name: Opera Queensland
funding: Not-for-profit company. Of $8.9M operating income in 2025, $4.3M was government grants, $2.0M sponsorship and donations and $1.7M event income (annual report).

overview: Queensland's state opera company, founded in 1981 as the Lyric Opera of Queensland with Queensland Government funding, after the Queensland Opera Company closed in December 1980; it was renamed Opera Queensland in 1996 (Wikipedia).

It moved its main-stage productions to the Queensland Performing Arts Centre in 1985, and since 1996 its offices and rehearsal studio have been in South Bank, shared with Queensland Conservatorium Griffith University (Wikipedia).
Its registered address is the Queensland Conservatorium Building, 140 Grey Street, South Bank; it is a company limited by guarantee, Opera Queensland Ltd, ABN 83 101 258 750 (2025 annual report).
Patrick Nolan has been CEO and Artistic Director since 2017, and the company tours regional and remote Queensland as well as performing in Brisbane (company website).
details.funding_verdict: Opera Queensland: government grants with family foundations and local corporate partners
funding: Operating income was $8,908,090 in 2025: grant income $4,316,786, sponsorships and donations $1,970,960, event income $1,731,600 and other income $888,774; 2024 operating income was $9,816,733 (2025 annual report).
Queensland Government: an operational grant of $2,860,319 in 2025 ($2,823,061 in 2024) plus $399,182 project funding and $61,963 Opera Conference funding (2025 financial statements).

Federal Government, through Creative Australia: an operational grant of $504,694 in 2025 plus $183,855 project funding and $272,273 Opera Conference funding; local government contributed $34,500 (2025 financial statements).
Government partners named for 2025 are Arts Queensland, Creative Australia, Brisbane City Council and Tourism and Events Queensland (2025 annual report).

The 2025 report lists Downtown Toyota as principal partner; Brisbane Racing Club, Haymans Electrical, Kawai, Shayher Group and Veracity as major partners; and the Frazer Family, Mather and Tim Fairfax Family foundations as philanthropy partners (2025 annual report).
The Tim Fairfax Family Foundation's partnership sustains the company's regional touring program (2025 annual report).
The partner page also names Morgans, Cisco, Brisbane Airport and The Clem Jones Foundation among current supporters (company website).

Earlier major partners were KPMG, McCullough Robertson and Datacom in 2016, and Datacom, John Villiers Trust, KPMG, Mather Foundation, PwC and Tim Fairfax Family Foundation in 2018 (2016 and 2018 annual reports).
wider_context: The Queensland ministerial diary records Russell Mitchell, General Manager of Opera Queensland, and Alison Smith of Rio Tinto meeting the Arts Minister, Ian Walker, on 20 November 2013 for a discussion on portfolio matters (Queensland Government ministerial diary, November 2013).
Rio Tinto does not appear in the partner lists of the 2016, 2018 or 2025 annual reports; no annual report for 2013 or 2014 was found to check (Opera Queensland annual reports).

case_notes.title: Queensland ministerial diary
case_notes.text: The Queensland ministerial diary records the Arts Minister, Ian Walker, meeting Russell Mitchell, general manager of Opera Queensland, and Alison Smith of Rio Tinto on 20 November 2013 for a discussion on portfolio matters; no Rio Tinto sponsorship of the company was found.

grade_basis: No flagged funder or funding protest on record, and the amounts are given.

name: Queensland Museum
funding: Queensland Government statutory body. Of $62.7M income in 2024-25, $43.6M was grants and contributions, mostly state recurrent; Shell's QGC business is a named partner (annual report).
watch: Shell's QGC business has paid the museum $10.25M since 2015 for the Future Makers STEM schools program, drawing legal objections and protests in 2025-26.
why_flagged: The museum's 2024-25 annual report names Shell's QGC business as Community Partner, Comms Declare reported $10.25M from it since 2015 (DeSmog, 7 December 2025), BHP funded a $7.6M partnership from 2018 (AFR via CAMD, 11 August 2018), and about 50 people protested outside the museum on 1 July 2026 (The Point).

overview: Founded on 20 January 1862 by the Queensland Philosophical Society; it opened at its current site in the Queensland Cultural Centre, South Bank, in 1986, and "Kurilpa" was added to its name in 2023 (Wikipedia).
The museum is the headquarters of a network that includes Rail Workshops in North Ipswich, Cobb+Co in Toowoomba, Tropics in Townsville and a collections and research centre at Hendra (Wikipedia).
Wikipedia gives the collection as over 15.2 million items (Wikipedia).
Kurilpa welcomed 2,057,172 visitors in 2024-25 (2024-25 annual report).

As of November 2018 the remains of 660 Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people were stored in a room at the Kurilpa site; the museum has returned ancestral remains and cultural property since the 1970s (Wikipedia).
details.funding_verdict: Queensland Museum: state-funded statutory body with fossil fuel and mining partners
funding: Income from continuing operations was $62.679 million in 2024-25, down from $66.022 million in 2023-24; grants and other contributions were $43.610 million, including $32.106 million in recurrent Queensland Government grants and $7.865 million in special state grants (2024-25 annual report).

The museum secured more than $2.11 million in cash and in-kind support from corporate partners in 2024-25, including $865,000 from 27 partners for World Science Festival Brisbane and Queensland (2024-25 annual report).

The 2024-25 report lists Shell's QGC business as Community Partner of the museum and of World Science Festival Brisbane, Energy Queensland as Reconciliation Partner and Powerlink as Regional Partner (2024-25 annual report).

Future Makers is described by the museum as "an innovative partnership between Queensland Museum and Shell's QGC business" for STEM learning, with teacher workshops in Gladstone and Chinchilla (museum website).

Comms Declare reported that Shell QGC has paid the museum $10.25 million since 2015 (DeSmog, Ellen Ormesher, 7 December 2025); the Arts Minister disclosed $800,000 for the 2024-25 Future Makers program in answer to a Greens question (AAP, Poppy Johnston).

BHP Billiton: a $1.4 million biodiversity partnership announced on 12 May 2015 by Premier and Arts Minister Annastacia Palaszczuk, who called it "the largest corporate partnership to date for the Museum" (mysunshinecoast.com via CAMD, 12 May 2015).

BHP: a $7.6 million partnership to digitise and 3D-scan the collection, starting with megafauna fossils found at BHP Mitsui Coal's South Walker Creek mine (Australian Financial Review via CAMD, 11 August 2018); the museum calls Project DIG a five-year partnership from 2018 to 2023 (museum website).

red_flags.heading: Fossil fuel sponsorship of school programs
points: Legal advice from the Environmental Defenders Office, commissioned by Comms Declare, found fossil fuel sponsorship "fundamentally incompatible" with the museum's legislated duty (Comms Declare, 19 September 2025).
CEO Jim Thompson wrote in October 2025 that the board carried out "comprehensive due diligence and risk assessment" before approving the partnership (DeSmog, 7 December 2025).

red_flags.heading: Protest or boycott
points: About 50 people, including representatives of the ACF, the Wilderness Society and Doctors for the Environment Australia, protested outside the museum on 1 July 2026, and an open letter signed by Tim Winton and others asked it to end its industry ties (The Point, Tegan George, 1 July 2026).

wider_context: The Australian Greens lodged a Senate motion for an inquiry into the fossil fuel industry's influence on children after a report counted more than 260 coal, oil and gas education initiatives and sponsorships nationwide (The Point, 1 July 2026).

case_notes.title: Queensland ministerial diary
case_notes.text: The Queensland ministerial diary records the Arts Minister, Leeanne Enoch, at a portfolio event with representatives of QGC, Shell's Queensland gas business, and of the Queensland Museum Network on 24 July 2018.

case_notes.text: The Queensland ministerial diary records the Arts Minister, Leeanne Enoch, at a portfolio event with Shell representatives, a Queensland Museum Network representative, the local MP Glenn Butcher and the Gladstone mayor on 2 March 2019.

grade_basis: A funder tied to fossil fuels. The record also holds a public protest.
